chapter: New Orleans bands: Cheek, Parker, Morgan
title: Percentage jobs and Thomas Jefferson working the door
summary: Playing on percentage, Morgan using his trumpeter to watch the door take, and what a night paid.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Right, right. Ike was playing for the Dove. Most of his job was in those days with percentage. Sometimes we'd get a cash job. Do you have any battles of music in there? I believe Ike played a battle with somebody. I ain't forgotten now.
How did that thing work with the Dove deal?
Explain that. Well, I'd work on 50-50 bands sometime 60-40.
Who'd get to 60?
We'd get to 60 and the man'd get to 40.
How could you do? You'd never know though.
I didn't know they was at the Dove right now.
I mean you'd never know if you'd get cheated or not.
You see Ike used to take Thomas to play trumpet. Huh? Isaiah Morgan used to take Thomas Jefferson to play trumpet. Did you play himself? Ike waked the Dove.
Oh, he waked the Dove. Yeah. Oh, he wanted to make sure that he got the right part.
Yeah. You had to have somebody to do that.
You had to have somebody that you could trust. You asked Thomas Jefferson about it.
You asked Thomas Jefferson about it. You asked Thomas Jefferson about it.
I see.

So, Thomas Jefferson would play? Yeah, he'd come and play after 12 o'clock after he'd see about, you know, it didn't look like too much could be gotten at the door, you know what I mean. Whatever the man would take at the door in, well it wouldn't be, if he would take it wouldn't be too much, you see, then Ike would come up and play. I see.
So you played at the last part of the job.
Mm-hmm.
So he was more like a businessman than a musician. Yeah.
Yeah, Thomas, that was his trumpet player. Oh yeah? Thomas Jefferson. I see.

So he wanted to make sure that nobody messed him up on the money, huh? Mm-hmm. Was that a very common thing in those days, to work the doors like that? Who? That was a common thing that, uh, all over, even in New Orleans too?
